subject: Network narrative + control map for Helio SIG/CAIQ review
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Network narrative + control map for Helio SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Alejandra / Helio team,

Thanks for the SIG/CAIQ heads-up — attached are the two items we discussed in the kickoff: a concise network narrative (Redwood_Private_Network_Story_v1.pdf) and a CAIQ control mapping workbook (CAIQ_Control_Map_Helio.xlsx). High-level notes in the narrative:

- We document both Dedicated (customer VPC peering or private interconnect) and Private (customer-managed VPC + private control plane) deployment models.
- Isolation model summary: tenant runtime is logically isolated with per-tenant KV cache namespaces; control plane is multitenant but runs in a separate AZ/NSG set with strict egress whitelists.
- Key controls mapped in the workbook: boundary diagrams to CAIQ network controls (SC-02, SC-07 equivalents), firewall/eBPF enforcement points, and KMS scoping.

Files attached: Redwood_Private_Network_Story_v1.pdf (2 pages narrative + 1 diagram), CAIQ_Control_Map_Helio.xlsx (tabbed mapping: CAIQ -> evidence location -> owner). Also included inline notes on which diagram pages correspond to the SIG templates.

Quick asks: could you confirm whether you want an additional physical rack-level diagram for Dedicated hardware (we can export a PDF from infra) and whether the SIG wants the one-page blast-radius statement as a standalone artifact or folded into the narrative?

If useful, David can jump on a short call to walk the architecture; Marissa will own delivery for the audit bundle.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Private_Network_Story_v1.pdf (application/pdf), CAIQ_Control_Map_Helio.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of clarifying items before we spin up the SIG template: 

1) Would you be able to provide separate logical and physical diagrams? Our risk team expects a logical flow for traffic and a separate high-level physical layout for Dedicated environments.
2) For Dedicated deployments, does Redwood allow customer-managed VPCs (Redwood peered) and also a Redwood-managed VPC option? We need both behavioral and ownership notes in the CAIQ fields.

Also — we have a one-page template for "blast radius" language we've used historically. Do you prefer we send our template and you fill it, or would you produce your own single-paragraph statement?

If it's easier, a 30-minute walkthrough early next week would help our reviewers.

Appreciate it,

Alejandra Ruiz

Hi Alejandra —

Quick answers from infra/architecture perspective: 

- Diagrams: we will provide both logical (sequence/flow) and a single high-level physical view for Dedicated. The logical diagram highlights per-tenant isolation points: request ingress -> routing layer -> per-model runtime pools -> KV cache namespaces -> egress gateway. The physical view shows AZ placement, peering/VPN termination, and optional private interconnect.

- Dedicated ownership models: Redwood supports two deployment patterns for Dedicated customers:
  * Customer-managed VPC (preferred for strict network control): customer provisions VPCs; Redwood establishes peering or private interconnect. Control owners are a mix: customer owns VPC-level NSG/ACLs; Redwood owns in-cluster routing and host-level firewall.
  * Redwood-managed VPC with dedicated subnetting: Redwood manages the VPC on behalf of the customer and enforces tenant fencing via software-defined network policies and host isolation.

- Blast-radius language: we can draft a single-paragraph statement capturing failure modes (control-plane separation, tenant eviction, KV cache scoping, egress-wormhole mitigation). I'll attach the segregation_runbook.md that contains the failure-mode bullets you can lift from.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wednesday 2027-01-13 10:00 PT to walk the two diagrams and the runbook. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,

David Kim
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: segregation_runbook.md (text/markdown)
